items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight to 'what day are you looking into moving?'
Never asked for origin or destination address/zip — customer volunteered cross streets ('Hardin and El Dorado') and he never captured a real address
Never asked home size, sq footage, bedrooms, stairs/floors, boxes, or access/parking
Never quoted an hourly rate — the only pricing mentioned was that the truck is included
No 2.5 hour minimum, no clock-starts-on-site, no 15-minute increments, no sense-check

No estimate at all — no time range, no number of movers, no dollar figure, despite having enough info (10x30 storage unit less than a mile away, boxes packed, China cabinet and dining table to disassemble)
No No Worries Damage Coverage, no Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee, no 'no hidden fees' pitch
Entire Save Your Ass speech skipped — and the customer teed it up perfectly with 'I just don't think I have enough stuff packed'
Never asked for the booking; ended with the customer saying she'd call back Monday. No deposit mention, no confirmation email, no 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never used the customer's name (Racquel) once after collecting and spelling it
Missed her urgency cues — 'they want us out by like the end of the month' and 'I can't take off the second day of school' — no acknowledgment, no attempt to problem-solve around them
top_strength: Handled the truck-size objection cleanly and confidently — explained the 26-foot box truck is the only size, that it's already baked into the hourly rate with no upcharge, and reframed why keeping the crew together beats splitting them across a sub-mile shuttle. That was the one moment he sounded like an expert.
coaching_note: This was a hot, ready-to-buy lead with a hard end-of-month deadline and Jules let her hang up without an address, a rate, an estimate, or a booking attempt. Next call: even on an inbound callback, run the full intake and build the estimate live on the phone — never end a sales call with 'call me back Monday.'
phone_presence_notes: Polite and easy to talk to, but purely transactional — zero name use, no affirmations, and he let two clear stress cues (end-of-month deadline, first week of school) pass without a word of empathy.
audio_review_reason: Transcript has garbled and dropped stretches (a stray 'Hello.' mid-conversation, several fragmented customer lines), so presence signal is thin — and given this was a lost booking on a ready buyer, the audio is worth a direct listen for coaching.
